question: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Samhita (BNSS), which court can grant default bail after the prescribed time limit?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Magistrate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Default bail**, also known as statutory bail, is granted under **Section 167(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)** when the investigating agency fails to complete the investigation within the prescribed time limit.
 
• Under the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Samhita (BNSS)**, the authority to grant default bail primarily lies with the **Magistrate**, who oversees cases within their jurisdiction.
 
• The prescribed time limit for completing investigations is **90 days** for offenses punishable with imprisonment of 10 years or more and **60 days** for other offenses, as per CrPC guidelines.
 
• If the investigating agency fails to file the charge sheet within this time frame, the accused becomes entitled to default bail, provided they apply for it.
 
• The **Magistrate** plays a crucial role in ensuring compliance with legal standards and safeguards the rights of the accused by granting default bail when conditions are met.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Samhita (BNSS):**

 
 
• The BNSS is a proposed codification aimed at simplifying and reorganizing various criminal procedural laws, including the **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)**.
 
• It emphasizes the protection of citizens’ rights while ensuring efficient criminal justice delivery.
 
• The BNSS aims to enhance transparency, reduce procedural delays, and improve access to justice for all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Role of Magistrate:**
 
 
• A Magistrate is a judicial officer empowered by law to handle cases related to criminal offenses, including the authority to grant bail.
 
• In the context of default bail, the Magistrate ensures adherence to the prescribed investigation time frame under **Section 167(2) of CrPC**.
 
• The Magistrate acts as the first level of judicial authority for criminal matters within their jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **Default Bail Mechanism:**
 
 
• It is a statutory right provided to the accused if the investigating authority fails to file the charge sheet within the stipulated time.
 
• The accused must apply for default bail, and the court must grant it if the conditions are fulfilled.
 
• Default bail ensures that investigation delays do not lead to indefinite custody of the accused, protecting their fundamental rights under the **Constitution of India**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Judicial Authorities:**
 
 
• **District Court:** Handles appeals and cases beyond the jurisdiction of Magistrates but does not directly grant default bail under CrPC.
 
• **High Court:** Acts as an appellate authority and can grant bail in exceptional cases, but default bail is typically handled by Magistrates.
 
• **Gram Nyayalaya:** A village-level court dealing with petty civil and criminal cases but does not handle default bail under CrPC.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Section 167(2) of CrPC:** Provides the legal framework for default bail, ensuring the rights of the accused are not compromised due to delays in investigation.
 
• **Constitutional Safeguards:** The right to default bail aligns with Article 21 of the **Constitution of India**, which guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty.
 
• **Judicial Precedents:** Various rulings by the **Supreme Court of India** have reinforced the importance of default bail as a statutory right of the accused.
